current_date: March 2026 (document text 'Bury Council Checklist Criteria March 2026'; approved by Planning Control Committee 24 March 2026)
current_evidence: The council's planning-application-process page links this file as 'Local criteria all developments validation checklist'. Its text is headed 'Bury Council Checklist Criteria March 2026', and the 24 March 2026 Planning Control Committee report approved it and merged the Places for Everyone checklist into it. The type-specific checklists (householder, advertisement, telecoms, waste, wind) are still dated 19 March 2024.

issues.detail: The list date 2026-05-01 comes from PDF metadata (Date basis 'PDF metadata CreationDate'). The document text says March 2026, and the committee approved it on 24 March 2026.
issues.evidence: Footer 'Bury Council Checklist Criteria March 2026'; PCC report 'Agenda item 8 PCC Report Validation March 2026' (meeting 24 March 2026)

issues.detail: Many numbered local criteria are missing from the application-type rows. Supporting Planning Policy Statement (item 1: all major, development not in accordance with the development plan). Affordable Housing Statement (item 3: 25 or more dwellings, or wherever affordable housing is provided, incl. Vacant Building Credit evidence). Sunlighting/Daylighting Assessment (item 4: new buildings of 4+ storeys adjoining developed land, or sites subject to significant shading). Parking and Servicing Details (item 8: all non-householder applications). Air Quality (item 9: AQMA-related). Retail Impact Assessment (item 10: significant change in retail floorspace, or retail over 2,500m2 gross). Refuse Disposal Details (item 17: new dwellings and new business/retail/food/pub/industrial/leisure uses). Crime Impact Statement (item 22: all major; 10+ residential units; student accommodation 6+ units; supported housing; 500m2+ office/industrial/retail/leisure etc.; hotels; licensed premises; car parks). Coal Mining Report (item 24: development breaking ground in Coal Authority high-risk areas). TV Impact Assessment (item 25: new buildings of 4+ storeys adjoining developed residential land). Heritage Statement for full applications in or affecting a conservation area or the setting of a listed building or scheduled monument (item 6; Grokbot captured it only under Listed building and Householder).
issues.evidence: Local criteria all developments checklist (March 2026), items 1, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 17, 22, 24, 25

issues.detail: None of the Places for Everyone requirements merged into the March 2026 list are captured. Carbon and Energy Statement (item 26: all major developments, all new buildings excluding householder, and change of use applications). Heat and Energy Statement (item 27: 10+ dwellings or new industrial development in Heat and Energy Network Opportunity Areas; it appears only as a fragment in tab_items). Nationally Described Space Standards table (item 28: all new dwellings). Density Statement (item 29: all new dwellings). Health Impact Assessment (item 30: EIA-screened development, new or improved health facilities, proposals with notable health impacts). Digital Connectivity Statement (item 31: all new buildings and all change of use applications, minor and major). Transport Assessment to consider the impact on Holcroft Moss (item 32, Policy JP-C8).
issues.evidence: Local criteria checklist items 26-32; PCC report s2.5: combine the local validation checklist and the Places for Everyone validation checklist into one

issues.detail: Advertisement is marked '(none)', but Bury publishes an advertisement consent checklist (19 March 2024), which Grokbot did not read. It requires scaled drawings (not less than 1:100) showing size, siting, materials, colour, height above ground, projection, and method and colours of illumination. It also requires a driver distraction assessment for LED advertisement hoardings. Householder also misses the tree survey for development within 2m of a tree canopy (item 14).
issues.evidence: advertisement-consent-applications-validation-checklist-march-2024.pdf, linked from the council's planning-application-process page; local criteria item 14

issues.detail: All four 'Change of use' rows (Block plan/Site plan, Landscaping, Pre-application advice, Telecommunications ICNIRP certificate) come from the Prior Approval for Telecommunications Equipment checklist, which does not apply to change of use applications. The local criteria requirements that do name change of use, the Carbon and Energy Statement and the Digital Connectivity Statement, are not listed there.
issues.evidence: Source of rows: prior-approval-telecommunications-equipment-march-2024.pdf; local criteria items 26 and 31 name change of use applications

issues.detail: Design and Access Statement is listed under Householder and Reserved matters using a fragment ('with the design and access statement. ___ Bury Council Checklist Criteria March 202'). That fragment comes from the heritage section's note that any DAS should include photographs. Item 1 requires a DAS only for major development, listed building consent, and conservation area development of one or more dwellings or over 100m2, not for householder applications generally.
issues.evidence: Local criteria item 1 (DAS triggers) and item 6 ('Any Design and Access Statement or Conservation Area Appraisal should be accompanied by appropriate photographs')

issues.detail: Several Full planning rows quote the wrong item. 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' quotes the Health Impact Assessment trigger ('...for an EIA. New developments that provide new or improved health facilities...'). 'Block plan / Site plan' quotes the Appendix 1 drainage layout plan list. 'Pre-application advice' quotes the S106 Heads of Terms text. 'Sunlight to gardens/amenity space' is actually item 5, Amenity Space/Recreational Provision (10 units over 1,000m2 or 11+ dwellings). 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' is the fragment 'intensity of illumination.' from External Lighting. 'Noise Impact Assessment' comes from the wind turbine checklist (noise and shadow flicker), not the general noise trigger in item 9.

The Flood Risk Assessment trigger ('where one is required') leaves out the actual triggers: Flood Zones 2/3 including minor development and change of use, sites over 1ha in Flood Zone 1, certain Flood Zone 1 changes to more vulnerable uses, and critical drainage areas. Several other excerpts include page footers ('______ Bury Council Checklist Criteria March 2026') or trailing item numbers.

Both Outline rows (BNG, Open space/play space) and one tab_item come from the March 2024 committee report (development-management-validation-checklist-criteria-report-march-2024.pdf), not a checklist. The quoted 'triggers' are report narrative such as 'a level playing field with no ambiguity over what is needed...'. Grokbot missed the actual outline-specific requirement: Appendix 1 minimum outline drainage information (outline drainage assessment and indicative drainage strategy).
issues.evidence: Local criteria Appendix 1 'Sustainable Drainage Pre-application Standing Advice' (outline and full application drainage requirements)

issues.detail: About 20 Full planning rows are marked 'INFERRED: application type not named', although the source sets triggers by development characteristic. Examples are Structural Survey (conversion of rural buildings in the Green Belt, unstable land, some listed building or conservation area cases) and Ventilation/Extraction (A3/A4/A5 premises and significant retail/business/leisure schemes). Employment Land applies to any proposal to redevelop employment land for another use, including outline.

Most of the 16 tab_items are not requirements. Examples are the footer line 'Bury Council Checklist Criteria 19 March 2024' and the report sentence 'The report outlines the review of the Council's local checklists...'. Others are 'These provisions consider a standardised basis for the submission of applications...', 'Bury Council encourages prospective developers to first contact the local planning authority...', 'For the majority of the Borough, standing advice will suffice.', 'SuDS can include a wide range of techniques...', 'The NPPF (and associated NPPG) related to Government policy...' and the optional wind turbine 'Community Benefits Consider the provision of a community benefit scheme'.
issues.evidence: tab_items sections 'Local forms / checklists' and 'Submission rules'

summary: The link is to the current, committee-approved March 2026 local criteria checklist, but the date comes from PDF metadata (May 2026). The extraction leaves out most of the 32 local criteria, including all the merged Places for Everyone items (carbon/energy, NDSS, density, HIA, digital connectivity, Holcroft Moss). It also took Change of use rows from the telecoms prior-approval checklist and missed the advertisement checklist entirely.
